transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi… thanks. I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a really hard time keeping up with basic adult responsibilities. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I keep forgetting things like paying bills, replying to interview emails, going to appointments, or finishing errands I said I’d do.

It’s started to actually cost me opportunities, which is kind of embarrassing. I thought I could just get more organized or try harder, but it’s not really working, so… I thought I should talk to someone.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in a major way, at least. I mean, I get frustrated with myself and kind of embarrassed when I mess things up, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed or that I don’t enjoy things anymore. I think it’s more the stress of not keeping up, if that makes sense.
Do you often find it hard to focus or stay attentive, even when you're trying your best, like during conversations, reading, or tasks that require sustained mental effort?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I try really hard, so I don’t want it to sound like I’m just not making an effort. But I’ll sit down to do something important, like update my resume or work on a coding practice problem, and then a text notification goes off, or someone is talking outside, or even just some random thought about another thing I need to do pops up, and suddenly I’m completely off track.

Sometimes I don’t even notice it happened until I’m already doing something else. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying still, especially in situations where you're expected to sit quietly or focus for a while?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I can usually make myself stay seated if I have to, so it’s not like I’m jumping up in the middle of things. But inside I feel really restless.

Like during an interview or a meeting, or even just sitting through a movie, I get this uncomfortable pressure in my body where I need to shift around or do something with my hands. If I don’t, I feel like I’m going to crawl out of my skin a little. I don’t know if that sounds dramatic, but that’s kind of what it feels like.
Do these difficulties with focus and restlessness happen in different parts of your life, like at home, at work, and in social situations, or are they limited to just one area?

Yeah… it’s not just one area, unfortunately. I wish it were, because then I could just fix that one thing.

It’s kind of showing up everywhere. Since I got fired, I’ve been trying to apply and interview and get things back on track, but I’ve missed follow-up emails after interviews or just… didn’t send things when I was supposed to. And I had this volunteer project I really cared about, and I ended up having to step back because I couldn’t keep up reliably.

I feel embarrassed saying that, because I don’t want it to sound like I don’t care. I do care. I just don’t seem to manage the basic steps consistently enough right now, and it makes moving forward feel really hard. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Looking back, were you already having trouble with focus, forgetfulness, or restlessness before you turned 12 years old, or did these issues start more recently?

Yeah… I think it was there pretty early, honestly. I don’t want to overstate it, because I did okay in school in some ways, but even in elementary school teachers would write things like I was bright, but I was always losing worksheets or couldn’t find assignments because my desk was such a mess.

I also remember getting comments about rushing through directions and talking out of turn. At the time I think people just thought I was messy or needed to try harder, but looking back… it does seem like this was happening before middle school. Is that helpful?
